title: Geometry optimization
action: Perform DFT geometry optimization for each Janus monolayer (γ-Pb₂SSe, γ-Pb₂STe, γ-Pb₂SeTe) using Quantum ESPRESSO with PBE PAW pseudopotentials and van der Waals corrections until forces are below 1×10⁻³ Ry/Bohr, with appropriate vacuum layer.

title: Electronic structure and effective mass calculation
action: From optimized structures, run SCF and band structure DFT (PBE). Extract effective masses of electrons and holes by parabolic fitting, and obtain Kohn-Sham eigenvalues on a dense k-mesh for BoltzTraP2.
description: Obtain PBE band structure and effective masses.

title: Harmonic phonon calculation
action: Compute second-order IFCs using Phonopy on a supercell. Use HiPhive to enforce rotational invariance (quadratic ZA mode). Obtain harmonic phonon frequencies.
description: Harmonic force constants for dynamic stability and anharmonic calculations.

title: Mechanical and deformation potential calculations
action: Apply uniaxial strains to the rectangular unit cell, relax ions, and extract 2D elastic modulus and deformation potentials for CBM/VBM from strain-energy and band edge shifts.
description: Determine elastic constants and deformation potentials needed for carrier mobility.

title: Carrier relaxation time from deformation potential theory
action: Using effective masses, 2D elastic modulus, and deformation potentials, compute carrier mobility and relaxation time τ via Bardeen–Shockley formula. Average over directions.
description: Derive relaxation time that scales electronic transport coefficients.

title: Lattice thermal conductivity by anharmonic phonon LBTE
action: Compute third-order IFCs with Phono3py on a supercell, then solve the phonon LBTE to obtain κ_l at 300 K and 800 K with thickness scaling.
description: Lattice thermal conductivity, a key component of total κ.

title: Electronic transport coefficients (BoltzTraP2 with DP τ)
action: Run BoltzTraP2 on the PBE band structure using the DP relaxation time τ to obtain S, σ, PF, and κ_e as functions of p-type carrier concentration and temperature (300–800 K).
description: Electronic transport properties needed for ZT.

title: Optimal p-type ZT extraction
action: Combine PF and κ_e from step 7 with κ_l from step 6 to compute ZT(n,T). For each monolayer, locate the p-type carrier concentration that maximizes ZT at 300 K and 800 K, and collect the corresponding transport parameters. Write a CSV with 6 rows.
description: Aggregate optimal p-type ZT and associated transport parameters.
